itemListElement.name: Board Minutes of Meeting in India: 2026 Format and Sample

mainEntity.name: What is the time limit for board minutes in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: SS-1 sets 15 days for draft minutes to reach directors and 7 days for their comments. Section 118 requires minutes to be prepared, signed and kept within 30 days. A certified copy of the signed minutes goes to directors within 15 days of signing.

mainEntity.name: Who signs board minutes of meeting?

acceptedAnswer.text: The chairperson of the meeting signs the minutes, or the next meeting's chairperson if needed. Usually the company secretary prepares them. Each meeting's minutes end with a dated, signed last page. Directors receive a certified copy of the signed minutes, so everyone works from one final record.

mainEntity.name: How long must board minutes be preserved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Board and committee meeting minutes must be preserved permanently, usually in the minutes book kept at the company's registered office. Keep supporting papers, such as notices and board packs, alongside them. Why? Auditors and due diligence teams usually ask for both together.

mainEntity.name: Can board minutes be changed after signing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Signed minutes should not be altered. Any correction should be approved at a later board meeting and recorded in that meeting's minutes. Never edit a signed page or use loose sheets. Fixes belong in the next meeting's minutes, which keeps the record trustworthy as evidence.

Board minutes are internal records. They are not public filings, but they may be inspected by directors, auditors and authorities, and some resolutions must be filed with the Registrar of Companies. Directors should treat them as confidential unless the board decides otherwise.

Yes. Companies may maintain minutes in electronic form subject to the applicable rules on security and signatures. Confirm the current requirements with your company secretary. Electronic minutes still need identical content, timelines and signatures to paper ones.
